messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

Thanks in advance for your help.  I'm using Subread 1.4.4 running the following:

featureCounts -T 12 -t exon -g gene_id -a SuperGenomeTest2.gtf -o microbial_gcounts \
/path/to/sample1/Aligned.sortedByCoord.out.bam \
/path/to/sample2/Aligned.sortedByCoord.out.bam

When my complete GTF looks like this:
SuperGenome    custom    gene    4287901662    4428583442    .    +    .    gene_id "Streptomyces";
SuperGenome    custom    exon    4287901662    4294743310    .    +    .    gene_id "Streptomyces"; transcript_id "Streptomyces_trans_1347"; exon_id "Streptomyces albus";
SuperGenome    custom    exon    4294967295    4303778917    .    +    .    gene_id "Streptomyces"; transcript_id "Streptomyces_trans_1348"; exon_id "Streptomyces averm";
I get these errors and warnings:

//================================= Running ==================================\\
||                                                                            ||
|| Load annotation file SuperGenomeTest2.gtf ...                              ||

Warning: the feature on the 2-th line has zero coordinate or zero lengths

Warning: the feature on the 3-th line has zero coordinate or zero lengths

||    Features : 2                                                            ||
featureCounts: readSummary.c:654: register_reverse_table: Assertion `this_block_min_start <= this_block_max_end' failed.
Aborted

However, if I change the position of that last exon start position by just 1 bp the error is gone:
GTF:
SuperGenome    custom    gene    4287901662    4428583442    .    +    .    gene_id "Streptomyces";
SuperGenome    custom    exon    4287901662    4294743310    .    +    .    gene_id "Streptomyces"; transcript_id "Streptomyces_trans_1347"; exon_id "Streptomyces albus";

//================================= Running ==================================\\

|| Load annotation file SuperGenomeTest2.gtf ...                              ||

Warning: the feature on the 2-th line has zero coordinate or zero lengths

Warning: the feature on the 3-th line has zero coordinate or zero lengths

||    Chromosomes : 1                                                         ||
||                                                                            ||
|| Process BAM file  ... ||
||    Single-end reads are included.                                          ||
||    Assign reads to features...                                             ||

What's more, if I change the position of all features, the warnings go away:
SuperGenome    custom    gene    5287901662    5428583442    .    +    .    gene_id "Streptomyces";
SuperGenome    custom    exon    5287901662    5294743310    .    +    .    gene_id "Streptomyces"; transcript_id "Streptomyces_trans_1347"; exon_id "Streptomyces albus";

Can anyone explain this??  It's causing a pipeline of mine to break and I can't figure out what the cause is.  Other features also give me the zero-length warning, but this is the only feature that causes featureCounts to break.

Thanks,
Kipp

messages.subject: Strange entry in subjunc BED files
messages.subject_clean: Strange entry in subjunc BED files
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

We have been using subjunc v1.4.6-p1 to process several hundred stranded paired-end RNASeq samples and every so often a *.junction.bed file has an invalid line that looks similar to:

Chr | StartLeftBlock | EndRightBlock | Junction_Name | nSupport | Strand | StartLeftBlock | EndRightBlock | Color | nBlocks | BlockSizes | BlockStarts

17 | 4294967245 | 6075 | JUNC00124422 | 3 | - | 4294967245 | 6075 | 0,255,255 | 2 | 69,65 | 0,6061

It always is chromosome 17 and the left coordinate is always invalid with respect to chromosome 17's length and the right coordinate is always much smaller than the left.

With the newest version of subjunc (v1.5.0-p1) valid BED files are produced for the affected samples, however more junctions are produced in general probably due to the

improvements in how paired-end reads are mapped as announced with version 1.5.0.

Has anyone seen this before?  We would prefer not to have to rerun all the samples with the newest version of subjunc unless absolutely necessary.  Would you suggest we simply remove the invalid lines from the junctions in the BED files?

We invoke subjunc as follows:

subjunc  -u  -i /path/to/reference  -r Sample_r1_fastq.gz  -R Sample_r2_fastq.gz  --gzFASTQinput  -o Sample.sam  -I 5  -n 10  -T 7  -H  -d 50  -D 600  -S fr  -m 3  -p 1  --allJunctions  --rg-id 1  --rg SM:Sample --rg PL:ILLUMINA  --rg LB:LIB_Sample  --trim5 3  --trim3 5

A representative FASTQ or BAM file could be provided offline if desired.

Thanks,

Dan

I was using featureCounts to count a set of short single-end reads, and there were more reads assigned when it was performed at meta-feature level (genes) than at feature level (exons). I am wondering if the meta-feature is a set of features (in this case just count exonic hits) or it is a range of positions (also including intronic hits)?

Thanks in advance for your help.

Kaiyang

messages.subject: Re: featureCounts -- Features and meta-features
messages.subject_clean: featureCounts -- Features and meta-features
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kaiyang,

Could you provide your commands for gene-level and exon-level counting? The parameters used in your commands affect how many reads are counted.

Mata-features are always the set of features, so for summarizing RNA-seq reads to genes or exons each gene includes a set of exons and it does not include intron regions.

Best wishes,
Wei

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to use featureCounts with the --largestOverlap option, but I'm not seeing the difference I was expecting, so I think I may be using it incorrectly. I'm using featureCounts 1.5.0-p1 and calling:

featureCounts -s 2 -p -f -t exon --largestOverlap -a mygtffile.gtf -o counts.txt fwd.bam rev.bam

The manual says "If specified, reads (or fragments) will be assigned to the target that has the largest number of overlapping bases." so I was expecting that a read overlapping more than one exon would be assigned to the exon it overlaps most. My data has reads overlapping multiple exons, but while my counts are higher with --largestOverlap, a lot of the overlapping reads are not counted.

What is the intended behaviour? Do I need to set additional options to use it?

Thanks

Kira

Hi Kira,

I cannot see anything you did wrong. If a read has the same number of overlapping bases with two exons, it will still not be counted. I think that is the reason why you still got a lot of unassigned overlapping reads.

You may take at the 'counts.txt.summary' file to see how many reads were unassigned due to ambiguity.

Cheers,
Wei

messages.body_plain:
Dear Kipp,

Sorry for taking so long to get back to you.

We think the problem was caused by those features that have extremely large coordinates. The upper limit on the chromosomal coordinates featureCounts can process is 2^31. But you have coordinates much bigger than this in your annotation.

Even if featureCounts can process these large coordinates, these features would not get counts because the coordinates in your bam file are less than 2^31.

Best wishes,
Wei

messages.body_plain:
Dear Daniel,

Sorry for my slow response.

Did you use the same parameters when you ran different version of Subjunc? I noticed you used '-n 10' and '-m 3' in your command, but I would suggest you to use the default setting (ie. '-n 14' and '-m 1') which should give you a better trade-off between sensitivity and specificity. Your setting is a bit too stringent for the detection of exon-exon junctions.

The '--allJunctions' parameter will instruct subjunc to detect both canonical (with GT/AG donor/receptor sites) and non-canonical splice sites. Do you need to detect non-canonical junctions?

I would suggest you to remap all your data with the latest version using the default -n and -m values. Also there is improvement in the mapping of PE reads in the latest version.

Hope this helps.

Best,
Wei

In the scenario I'm working with, this behaviour is not very helpful, and at the moment I've modified my local version of the featureCounts code to assign such reads randomly to one of the exons which is overlapped. Hi Baptiste,

I guess you performed a gene-level read counting, which returns you a single number for each gene for each library. This number is the total number of reads overlapping with any exons in a gene.

If you want to count reads for each individual exon, you will need to specify '-f'.

Cheers,

No, not really - what I'm doing means I know each read has only been assigned to one exon, so, for example, I can sum across all the exons which overlap exactly to get a count.
